records.title: A significant step backwards in usability!
records.review:
The latest update to the Barclays app has made the main account screen significantly worse for anyone who uses multiple accounts.

Previously, when I opened the app I could immediately see my accounts in the order I had chosen, with my account nicknames clearly displayed. This made it incredibly easy to distinguish between accounts used for different purposes — for example, joint bills, household spending and other expenses.

The new interface instead prioritises a combined balance, which is of very little use to me. What I actually want to know at a glance is how much is in each individual account.

More frustratingly, account nicknames have disappeared from current accounts and the accounts are now automatically ordered by balance. This means their position can continually change as money moves in and out. Removing both the nickname and a consistent position makes identifying the right account unnecessarily difficult.

This is basic UX. Users develop familiarity with where their accounts are and use nicknames specifically to make them instantly recognisable. Taking away both of those things creates additional friction where there previously wasn’t any.

Barclays already feels significantly behind other major UK banks in terms of app development, so it’s disappointing to see development time being spent on an update that actually removes useful functionality.

Please restore account nicknames and allow customers to choose the order in which their accounts appear. A combined balance can be useful for those who want it, but it shouldn’t come at the expense of basic account visibility and personalisation.

And please make the massive leaps forward required to align your app with high street rivals like Lloyds and NatWest. Development pace is embarrassing and development decisions are painfully illogical.

You can’t paste anything into it — not an account number, an amount, or a company name — when making a payment (pasting data is far less likely to cause an error than typing it manually). The settings are also scattered all over the place, so I end up spending half an hour just trying to find where to update a detail or adjust a setting. When you try to submit feedback, it simply returns an error along the lines of “Oops, something went wrong — no email account is set up on this phone,” without explaining how to actually set one up. You also can’t change your PIN length (I’d prefer a 6-digit PIN). On top of that, there’s no chat or email-style messaging system; the only way to contact them is by phone, which is counterproductive, as I’d much prefer an asynchronous option.

After being disappointed with NatWest’s declining customer services and early branch closures, took the plunge and made Barclays my primary bank. This was a culture shock app wise as NatWest had been one of the pioneering banks and Barclays wasn’t quite there at the time! 

However this has changed happily over the past 5 years and it’s been a fantastic tool when it’s works which is 80% of occasions. 

Recently a series of updates have oddly required a full reset of the app which then requires you to use a sentry device…. Not a problem if banks (including Barclays) hadn’t started phasing them out years back in favour of using your smart phone! 

Ironically it doesn’t work as the app has been reset so this results in you going into branch if your unfortunate enough not to have a manual sentry device or one with battery left after then years of not being used (I found out the hard way once)!

Fortunately this usually happens maybe once or twice a year (although smaller updates are frequent and don’t need or cause a full reset). 

Overall it gets 4/5 as pretty solid App.
